s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive lower limb weakness with fluctuating course and spinal involvement
salient_findings: Ascending spastic weakness of the lower limbs
key_facts: 18-year-old man
6 months of fluctuating lower-limb weakness
Initial episode of leg weakness resolved over 30 minutes
Asymptomatic for 4 months
Developed ascending spastic weakness over 3 months
Urinary retention requiring a Foley catheter
One month of constipation
No trauma, fever, steroid or other drug intake, or infections
Normal routine hematological and biochemical tests
Normal cerebrospinal fluid analysis
Unremarkable plain radiographs of the spine
Posterior epidural mass from D5 to D7 on MRI

shortlist.label: Spinal epidural lipomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Posterior epidural mass with homogeneous hyperintensity on MRI, suggestive of fat

shortlist.label: Spinal cord compression
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive lower limb weakness with spinal involvement and evidence of cord compression on MRI

shortlist.label: Spinal epidural abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Fluctuating course and spinal involvement, although normal cerebrospinal fluid analysis reduces likelihood

shortlist.label: Spinal lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Posterior epidural mass with characteristics of fat on MRI, possible spinal lipoma

shortlist.label: Elusive spinal epidural angiolipomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Epidural mass with fat characteristics and possible vascular component, rare but plausible diagnosis

raw.rationale: The MRI findings of a posterior epidural mass from D5 to D7 that is homogeneously hyperintense on both T1-weighted and T2-weighted sequences, suggestive of fat, align with the characteristics of spinal epidural lipomatosis.

rejected.label: Spinal cord compression
rejected.why: While spinal cord compression could explain some symptoms, the specific MRI findings of a fatty mass are more indicative of spinal epidural lipomatosis.

rejected.label: Spinal epidural abscess
rejected.why: The absence of fever, infection, or abnormal cerebrospinal fluid analysis makes an abscess less likely.

rejected.label: Spinal lipoma
rejected.why: Although a lipoma could present similarly, the specific location and description as a posterior epidural mass suggest spinal epidural lipomatosis.

rejected.label: Elusive spinal epidural angiolipomatosis
rejected.why: This condition is less commonly referenced and the provided information does not specifically suggest angiolipomatosis over lipomatosis.
